narrative.overview:
One open account book, hinged on a centre gutter, kept by a clerk who posts everything twice. The left page carries what was missing in red and the right page carries what shipped in black. Coloured form stock, ruled feint, column rules, rubber stamps and marbled edges are the whole material vocabulary, and each of them is doing a job a real ledger would give it.

The system is loud in colour and strict in measure. Stock is saturated and changes with every folio, Besley Black runs at poster scale, and photographic cut-outs of Ali stand on the rules like paper puppets. Against that, every line of text sits on one ruled row and state is carried by ink: a posted entry gets heavier, a refused line is struck through, an approval is stamped. Nothing is erased; corrections are struck and stay on the page.

Two layouts express the same book. The book layout fills the viewport with a 25-row spread and turns real leaves on scroll, while the stacked layout gives phones, narrow or short windows, reduced motion and no-script visitors the complete content as a continuous run of ruled sheets.
keyCharacteristics: One form stock per folio, with ink and accent re-bound to each stock.
A single ruled row height as the unit of measure.
Besley Black display, Besley text on the rules, Courier Prime for posted figures, one clerk's hand.
Depth comes from paper physics: gutter crease, leaf turn, fore-edge, never a raised panel.
State lives in the ink and the stamp, not in badges or chips.

rules.name: The One Stock Per Folio Rule
rules.body: A folio is one form stock from edge to edge, both pages. Change stock only by turning to a new folio. Green may return to close the book; no other stock repeats.

rules.name: The Rebound Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink, accent, feint and column rule are set per stock as a group. Never carry one stock's accent onto another.

rules.name: The Debit And Credit Rule
rules.body: Accent ink means the debit side: what was missing, what was refused, what is still to be signed. Black or ivory ink means what shipped.

rules.name: The On The Rule Rule
rules.body: Running text has a line-height of exactly one row, so baselines sit on the feint. Never set body text on a free line-height.

rules.name: The Clerk's Hand Rule
rules.body: Homemade Apple is what the clerk writes by hand: the "what was missing" and "what shipped" T-account heads, signer marks, the payroll names, the sign-off lines, whatever a visitor types into the entry, and the staff's notes. Printed table heads stay in Besley. Never use the hand for running text or an action.

rules.name: The Figures Are Posted Rule
rules.body: Amounts in a working ledger are set in Courier Prime. Besley carries an amount only when it is a headline fact: a T-account posting or the one monumental figure on a spread.

rules.name: The One Row Rule
rules.body: Every element is measured against the ruled row: widths and offsets of stamps, heights of actions and fields, tab insets, corners, margins. In the book layout this is literal, and offsets may be fractions of a row. In the stacked layout gaps and controls use whole or half rows, and only viewport-sized display type leaves the rules.

rules.name: The Only Map Rule
rules.body: The thumb-index tabs are the only index of the book, one tab per folio in strict order, coloured with the stock they open. Page corners only turn to the next leaf, and an inline folio reference only cites its entry. Never add a second navigation, menu or table of contents.

rules.name: The Leaf Edge Rule
rules.body: In the stacked layout a cast shadow exists only where a sheet physically passes over a photograph. Sheets that follow one another on paper cast nothing.

rules.name: The Pasted Not Floating Rule
rules.body: A plate is pasted to the page: flat, bordered, shadowless. No element becomes a floating card.

dos: Do give each folio one form stock and bind its ink, accent, feint and column rule together.
Do measure stamps, controls, margins and offsets in rows.
Do post data to T-accounts and ruled line ledgers on the rows.
Do use the clerk's hand for what a person writes on the form, and Besley for what is printed on it.
Do show state in the ink: heavier when posted, struck through when refused, stamped when approved.
Do keep every correction visible; the book is append-only.
Do make ink texture and paper texture from raster images, as the stamps, grain and marbling already are.
Do keep the complete content available in the stacked layout for phones, reduced motion and no script.
donts: Don't imitate stamp ink with CSS filters, SVG filters or blend modes.
Don't add floating cards, raised panels, pills, chips, icon tiles or badges.
Don't add a second map of the book beside the thumb-index tabs.
Don't put a cast shadow on stacked sheets unless a sheet is passing over a photograph.
Don't repeat a stock on the next folio, or mix two stocks in one folio.
Don't round anything except the outer corners of a thumb tab.
Don't set running text off the row.
